name: Prize crossword No 22,601
preamble: Solve the clues and fit the solutions into the diagram jigsaw-wise, wherever they will go.

clue.text: High revelling is reported by bringers of bad luck

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word spoken the same

blocks.note: high jinks is boisterous fun, so the revelling word is jinks

explanation.surface: Noisy partygoers are blamed for bringing misfortune on everyone around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' belongs to the phrase high jinks; only the jinks part is sounded out.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a person or thing thought to cause misfortune, so the plural names several such carriers of ill fortune.

clue.text: Club for unhappy souls?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the metal that, in the old phrase, enters the soul of a sufferer

blocks.note: first meaning: a metal-headed golf club
second meaning: the metal of the Prayer Book psalm that 'entered into his soul', meaning bitter suffering

explanation.surface: A support group where the sad and lonely can meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Club is a golf club; the old phrase 'the iron entered into his soul' describes deep anguish, hence unhappy souls.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers carry several metal-headed clubs numbered by loft, each called by the metal name.

clue.text: Unknown object that wears down mother, needing moisturiser?

definitions.note: the clue gives a description of the condition; the answer is the noun for that condition

blocks.note: X is the classic unknown quantity in algebra
something that wears away is an eroder
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mystery item that grinds Mum down, and leaves her reaching for the hand cream.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical term for abnormally dry skin, a condition that cries out for an emollient cream.

clue.text: Kate's dance has cast about one to two thousand

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed around the others

blocks.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them

explanation.surface: A woman's party piece involves throwing something across a huge crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The old song goes 'I wish I could shimmy like my sister Kate'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's sister Kate famously performed a shaking jazz-age dance of the shoulders and hips.

clue.text: Sound of bird: get on with it, says Woy

indicators.note: we hear the phrase in the voice of someone who pronounces r as w

blocks.note: 'get cracking' means get on with it; spoken with a w for the r it becomes cwacking

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher reports a call while a politician urges everyone to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: Woy is how the British politician Roy Jenkins was mocked for saying his own name, as he could not pronounce r.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks make a harsh nasal call, and that noise is what a duck does when it calls out.

clue.text: Moon, M's coloratura part

blocks.note: first meaning: a poetic title for the moon, ruling the dark sky
second meaning: the high-soprano role in Mozart's opera The Magic Flute

explanation.walkthrough: M is this puzzle's shorthand for Mozart, the composer at 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon presides over the dark hours, and Mozart's villainous soprano in The Magic Flute bears that same regal title.

clue.text: Let in, I must confess

definitions.note: a phrase of concession, standing for the one-word concession that opens a sentence

blocks.note: first meaning: allowed to enter
second meaning: a word granting a point, as in 'granted, I was late'

explanation.surface: A doorman owns up to having allowed someone inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing entry and confessing a fault are both expressed by the same past-tense verb meaning owned up or permitted entrance.

clue.text: Job's second for king (English) and general (Pakistani)

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
standard abbreviation
General Zia-ul-Haq ruled Pakistan from 1977 to 1988

explanation.surface: Reads like a cast list where the deputy stands in for a king and a general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a moment or a deputy, but it means Job's second daughter in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: After his trials, Job had three new daughters, and the Bible names the middle one with this spelling variant.

clue.text: Cops nearly rattled when one drops off

definitions.note: a description of the condition; the answer is its noun

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: Police officers are almost rattled when someone collapses in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' looks like it trims a word, but here it is simply part of the letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a disorder in which sufferers fall suddenly asleep without warning at any time of day.

clue.text: This is the alternative to the solver's money

definitions.text: This is the alternative to the solver's money

blocks.clueFragment: This is the alternative to the solver's money
blocks.note: surface reading: some other option besides paying the puzzler
setter's reading: the highwayman's demand 'your money or ...', with the solver addressed as you

explanation.surface: Sounds like a choice about how a crossword winner is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: The highwayman's challenge offers two choices, and the solver is the 'you' being held up.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic robber's ultimatum puts survival of the victim as the only other option besides handing over cash.

clue.text: Reversing car in which is Australian composer

indicators.note: reversing makes the vehicle word run backwards
says the next item sits inside the one already given

blocks.note: a tram is a street rail car
Oz is slang for Australia

explanation.surface: An Australian musician is behind the wheel, backing the car out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salzburg-born genius wrote over six hundred works, including The Magic Flute and Don Giovanni.

clue.text: A devil at turning pastries, or one with a placard

indicators.note: turning round makes the baked goods word run backwards

blocks.note: a demon is a devil
tarts are pastries
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked figure flipping pastries in a kitchen, or else a protester with a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester marching at a rally typically carries a sign or banner showing the cause.

clue.text: One way to alter sound: twist of a tail's within the limit

definitions.note: the clue describes the process; the answer is the verb for doing it

indicators.note: a twist distorts the following letters into a new order
says the jumbled letters go inside the boundary word

blocks.note: a pale is a boundary, as in 'beyond the pale'
the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Twisting an animal's tail produces a different noise, though only up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, to shift a consonant's articulation toward the hard roof of the mouth changes its sound.

clue.text: Very common feature of fur in the squirrel

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
an air is a look or bearing, and air is shared by everyone

explanation.surface: Fur is a very common trait of squirrels.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a heraldic and medieval term for squirrel pelts, blue-grey and white, used to trim robes.

clue.text: Villein backing queen gets directions for first years

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the serf word runs backwards

blocks.note: a villein was a feudal serf
Her Majesty
east and north, two compass points

explanation.surface: A peasant supports the queen and is given orders to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Students in their initial year at university or college are commonly known by this term.

clue.text: Leave coat and hat here in hospital: on your feet, everyone!

definitions.note: the clue describes the furniture's use; the answer is the item's name

blocks.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
the order for the whole room to rise

explanation.surface: A ward visitor is told to leave outdoor clothes behind before all rise for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture in an entrance passage with hooks and often a mirror, where visitors drop outdoor clothing.

clue.text: Quality of M's Titus, the goalkeeper

blocks.note: first meaning: the mercy shown in Mozart's opera La Clemenza di Tito
second meaning: Ray ..., the Liverpool and England goalkeeper

explanation.walkthrough: M again stands for Mozart; the archaic word for mercy happens to be the surname of a famous England keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's emperor Titus shows mercy, an old form of which matches the surname of a celebrated 1970s keeper.

clue.text: Male god of the West Bank

definitions.note: the answer is a city located there

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
the Arabic name for God

explanation.surface: A masculine deity worshipped in the Palestinian territories.
explanation.definitionFit: The city serves as the administrative centre of the Palestinian Authority in the occupied territory west of the Jordan.

clue.text: End of Italian film without actors in training

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: La Strada is Fellini's 1954 film
the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school

explanation.surface: The close of a foreign movie made with no professional cast.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's leading drama school, so its students are actors in training.
explanation.definitionFit: The final item or moment in a series is its concluding one, a synonym for the close.

clue.text: Lose an ounce, possibly, with enthusiasm

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
oz is the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: A dieter eagerly hopes to shed a little weight.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Italian musical direction telling the performer to play zealously and fervently.

clue.text: Cooling jars with a period at the piano?

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written
a term is a period of time
a pianist plays on the keys

explanation.surface: Chilled pots placed beside a pianist during a practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the odd reading of 'at the piano' as being on its keys.
explanation.definitionFit: These are porous earthenware vessels used in hot countries, where evaporation through the clay keeps drinking supplies cool.

clue.text: Weapon taken from Kirklees to Calderdale

indicators.note: the letters are lifted out of the run of place names that follows

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first name, the small word, and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A weapon carried from one Yorkshire district to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: Kirklees and Calderdale are neighbouring local-government districts in West Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long thrusting sword of the late medieval period, designed to pierce armour.

clue.text: Spoil international party?

blocks.note: the United Nations is an international body
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Wrecking a global celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin or reverse someone's work is to destroy its effect, a sense of the verb meaning wreck.

clue.text: Shy shy?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone very timid, or a double throw
setter's reading: shy twice over, recalling the proverb about being cautious after a bad experience

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'once ..., twice shy': two shys point back to the first half of the saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a person once hurt is doubly wary, so the doubled shyness points back to the earlier hurt.

clue.text: M's fellow soldier has round five years in Rome

blocks.note: an American private soldier
a round shape
the Roman numeral for five
the Italian word for years

explanation.surface: A comrade in arms has spent five years stationed in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: M is Mozart, whose seducer hero is Don Giovanni.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera is named after the libertine Don, the man at its centre.

clue.text: Art instructor used to pack?

definitions.note: read as archaic 'thou art' one who instructs, the old second-person verb form

blocks.note: first meaning: 'thou art instructor' is 'thou' plus the old form of teach with -est
second meaning: a wooden crate for shipping and for house moves

explanation.surface: An art teacher drafted in to help with packing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the archaic verb as in 'thou art'; the -est ending is the old second-person form of a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plywood box lined with foil, originally for shipping leaves from Asia, later the standard crate for moving house.

clue.text: Bloody awful man?

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated verdict on some dreadful chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A former pupil of a school, or a familiar term of address for a chap, both refer to a male person.
